messages:
anja: Quick async check-in for the runtime perf milestone — short list of open items and owners. Please reply with ✅ when you’ve picked up anything. TL;DR: kernel PRs, continuous-batching canary, KV warmup eviction tweak, CI noise.
lee: I can take another look at kernel PR #3124 but CI is flapping on gpu-integration tests. Seeing CUDA OOMs occasionally.
maria: @lee I’ll queue a CI debug run on the 3124 branch and look at the test harness config. If we don’t stabilize, we should split the heavy integration test into separate shards.
lee: thanks — failing lines are here: ```
E tensorflow: OutOfMemoryError: Resource exhausted when allocating tensor with shape [8,4096,4096]
   at runtime/kernel/attention.cc:427
```
sam: FYI I filed issue RW-1289 for the CI flakiness and linked the debug logs (https://gitlab.redwood/rw/issues/1289). Will add a reproducible recipe there.
tony: I own the eviction heuristics work. Plan is to land PR #3130 today with a smaller LRU window to reduce cold-token misses. Canary target tomorrow AM.
anja: @tony please confirm the rollback plan if canary latency regresses >5% — we’ll want auto-fallback to previous evict policy.
ton﻿y: yes — rollback is implemented in router rule 'evict-policy-v1' with immediate fallback. I’ll add the canary flag `--evict-window=128` to the rollout.
maria: I volunteered to pick up the continuous-batching tuning doc updates (perf playbook). Will open a doc PR and a small config PR to change default batch_time_ms from 6 -> 4 for the canary.
lee: re: kernel PRs — I queued a perf microbenchmark against the new attention op. Results look good for short seqs, worse for long seqs. Need a knob to switch kernels based on seq len distribution.
anja: that’s fine — add a kernel selector that uses seq_len threshold 1024 for fallback. Add tests and a flag gate so we can flip remotely.
sam: ps — I kicked off a dedicated cluster canary (tag: runtime-canary-2026-03-05) via build-bot. build-bot: deployment scheduled to 3 nodes in us-west-2 at 09:00 UTC.
ops-bot: Canary cluster runtime-canary-2026-03-05 is UP. Health checks: 98% passing, 2 pods restarting (kernel-worker-7).
lee: I’ll grab logs from kernel-worker-7 and paste short snippet in the issue. If those restarts are due to OOMs we should throttle prefetch for initial warmup.
maria: I’ll update the KV warmup script to prefetch with a lower concurrency and add jitter. That should smooth coldstart spikes.
anja: Ownership recap: kernel PR #3124 -> lee (CI debug), PR #3130 -> tony (eviction), batching config -> maria, CI issue RW-1289 -> sam. Dependencies: CI stability + kernel test fixes before we flip canary flags.
lee: got it. I’ll post a short follow-up with the failing stack and a link to my draft fix.
sam: pinging infra to watch the canary window 09:00-12:00 UTC — please annotate any anomalies in RW-ops Slack channel.
anja: Awesome — if nobody objects I’ll mark this milestone as "on-track but CI-risk" and move the blocker tag to RW-1289. Please react with :thumbsup: when you’ve actioned your item.
maria: ✅
lee: ✅ (will update in ~45m)
tony: ✅ planning to merge after perf smoke pass
sam: ✅ I’ll keep the issue updated with infra observations
ops-bot: Note: Next automated rollback check at 09:30 UTC.
build-bot: CI re-run started for branch kernel/3124.
anja: Thanks all — short standup later if needed. If you hit a hard blocker, @anja DM.
